content.thinking:
Reviewing `listOrgIdsForRollup`, organization listings, and notification preference filtering.

Three issue counting bugs found. Project card counts miss canceled issues because closed status is not included. Overdue counts include done and canceled items instead of only open, non-archived issues past due. Reopening an issue fails to clear completedAt.

Closing an issue always sets a new completion stamp. Reopening it should clear completedAt to null. Start dates correctly remain fixed at the first in-progress time. The overdue sweep uses strict less-than, so issues due exactly at the current moment are not overdue.

The sweep's workspace listing may omit new workspaces or include deleted ones. The deduplication rule is now clear: an issue is announced only on the first sweep that finds it overdue, and it can be announced again once it is no longer overdue.

The deduplication logic needs to remove IDs from the reported set that were absent in the current sweep. A concern remains about issues announced before their workspace was deleted.

The sweep deduplication logic is now concrete. A `seenThisPass` set will track every issue found overdue in the current pass. Only issues missing from both that set and the persistent `reported` set will be announced.

The notify call uses the wrong event type: it should be `issue_due_soon` instead of `issue_overdue`. A null `dueAt` correctly excludes an issue from the overdue list.
Need a way to list all non-deleted organizations.

An overdue job comment requires calling `emit` and `shouldFilterArchived` directly instead of reimplementing them.

The job should query organizations directly where `archivedAt` is null instead of using `usageRepo`. The 50-org batch limit causes brand-new workspaces to be missed because they lack usage rows, and deleted workspaces to be included because their usage rows persist.

The 50-org batch limit should be removed entirely so no non-archived workspace is skipped. I also need to verify the Drizzle imports for `livePredicate` and `notInArray`, check the equality logic in `isOverdue`, and confirm that alerts are scoped to their own workspace.

Evaluating Drizzle ORM query patterns to filter records by open statuses, considering notInArray, or(ne, ne), and inArray.

Importing CLOSED_ISSUE_STATUSES into issue-repository and project-repository. The setIssueStatus logic will set completedAt to the current timestamp when entering a terminal status, or clear it when reopening. For project stats, using Drizzle's notInArray or inArray.

Overdue issues will use `notInArray` against closed statuses, or a double `ne` check. Archived records are already excluded by the live predicate. Strict `lt` comparisons ensure exact-due-time issues are not marked overdue. A new `listLiveOrgIds` helper will be added to the organization repository using `isNull(archivedAt)`.

The job already calls `shouldFilterArchived` via an early return. For querying organizations, using `livePredicate` directly in the job file is possible, but adding a `listLiveOrgIds` helper to the organization repository is cleaner.

Adding a new exported function is unlikely to break snapshot tests. The overdue job can import the organization repository directly. The ORG_BATCH limit will be removed since every live organization will be covered, and the constant will be deleted if unused. The usageRepo import will also be removed if it becomes unused. The tracking algorithm must also handle issues reported by organizations excluded from this sweep.

All organizations will be included in the sweep. Issues tied to deleted organizations are pruned by the end-of-sweep cleanup. Closed overdue issues are removed from reported because they were never seen this pass; they will be re-announced when they become overdue again. The tracking algorithm adds every issue to seenThisPass even if it is skipped because already reported. If emission fails, the issue is still added to seenThisPass but not to reported.

The notification kind is changing to `issue_overdue`. The tracking reset function clears the reported set, and tests call it between runs. The seen set is local to each run.
Checking member lookup by user in the organization to enforce workspace notification boundaries.

The optimistic reducer preserves the existing completedAt timestamp when closing again if it was already set.

The server path keeps the existing completion date when reopening, but it should clear it. The optimistic reducer already clears the date on reopen, yet it incorrectly preserves the old timestamp when closing again.

Updating `withStatus` to set `completedAt` to the current date on every close.

`completedAt` will be null for non-terminal statuses and stamped only when terminal. The server `setIssueStatus` layer is the authority. Adding a membership check to the overdue subscriber so alerts stay within the workspace.

The existing "does not re-emit" test still passes with the current algorithm if the issue remains overdue.

Listing all orgs instead of usage-based ones would scan more organizations. Jobs.test might pick up overdue issues from other tests if the database is shared. Tests expecting processed === 1 could fail. Each test file likely uses a temporary database.

Existing tests depend on usage rows.

The "emits once" test expects processed to equal 1. Previous tests already created overdue issues that remain in the database. Those prior emissions are still counted as overdue, so the expected count of one is likely wrong.

The reported Set tracks previously emitted issues across tests. processed counts only new emissions, so the "emits once" test passes despite prior overdue issues remaining in the database. The "does not re-emit" test correctly excludes those prior issues because they are already in the reported set. Issues closed before the job runs are never added to the reported set, so they remain selectable.

I will implement `listLiveOrgIds` using Drizzle's `notInArray` for SQLite. The overdue query will use `CLOSED_ISSUE_STATUSES` instead of a direct `ne done` check. Overdue stats already exclude archived issues and require a passed due date. I am also verifying that optimistic status updates correctly clear the completion date when reopening an issue.
Checking the `isOverdue` equality boundary for consistency between the job and date helper.

The `isOverdue` check uses strict less-than comparison.

Adding `listActiveOrgIds` to the organization repository. Pruning will visit all organizations even when errors occur. Deleted workspaces are excluded via `archivedAt`. Usage-based listings naturally handle orphan usage rows and brand new organizations.

Importing `CLOSED_ISSUE_STATUSES` into the issue repository to replace the local `TERMINAL_STATUSES` constant. The `completedAt` assignment will use this imported array, though a type assertion may be needed since `IssueStatus` is broader than the readonly closed subset.

Keeping the existing `TERMINAL_STATUSES` constant to avoid TypeScript type errors. The `completedAt` assignment will simply set it to null for non-terminal statuses.

For overdue issue queries, using Drizzle's `notInArray` against `CLOSED_ISSUE_STATUSES`. The project repository will also import `inArray` and `CLOSED_ISSUE_STATUSES`.

Using livePredicate so shouldFilterArchived is the source of truth for "not deleted".

Using isNull(organizations.archivedAt) in the org repo to match findOrgBySlug and archiveOrg. Checking member status "removed" versus archived. Implementing overdue issue tracking with a Set to avoid duplicate processing.

If an issue emit fails, it stays in stillOverdue and retries next cycle. After processing, reported issues are pruned if they are no longer overdue.

A partial failure in listOverdueIssues could cause incorrect pruning of reported issue IDs. The job will throw on failure instead, which is acceptable because it prevents re-announcing issues. The reported set only stores issue IDs, not organization IDs.

The reported set is only pruned after a complete successful sweep. If the job aborts mid-loop, unscanned issues remain reported and newly announced ones stay in place until the next full run. This conservative approach prevents re-announcing issues prematurely.

Canceled issues will be excluded from the overdue list. The optimistic reducer now sets `completedAt` to a new timestamp on every close, so reopening an issue updates its UI state. Existing tests for first closes remain valid.
Checking whether updateIssue can change issue status without calling setIssueStatus.
Status updates flow exclusively through setIssueStatus.
Checking overdue job lookahead constants to see if the window includes future dates.

OVERDUE_LOOKAHEAD_HOURS exists but the job does not use it.

Overdue alerts will only trigger for past-due issues and exact sweep times. Future issues are excluded. The comparison uses strict less-than to avoid boundary bugs. Alerts will be gated by workspace membership so notifications stay inside the correct organization.

Adding a membership check to keep alerts within their own workspace.

Fixing notification kind to resolve the "due soon" inbox filter issue. Updating the optimistic reducer to always use `at` when closing items so re-closing generates a new date.

Confirmed the completedAt test passes with null initial state. Canceled issues now receive a fresh completion date. Closed counts use `inArray` and overdue checks use `notInArray` against the closed status set. Archived issues remain excluded by scope.
